chapter: Royal Roost, Birdland and Three O'Clock High
title: Addiction among Royal Roost players and back with Slam at Bop City
summary: Collins names J. J. Johnson as having beaten heroin, then rejoined Slam Stewart at Bop City.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: But any way -- the Royal Roost was quite a place, you know, quite a club. Ralph Watkins and Irving Alexander, I believe, and Monte Kay. Monte Kay, they had this. And this particular band as I said was like an all star band. But everybody in there was junkies. You know, I guess Cecil Paine and -- well, just a lot of the guys I won't name. You know, some of them have beat it now so this is why I won't --

Yeah, well J. J. for one. You know, J. J. was one of the biggest -- he was really a junkie. But I admired him because he beat it and he was a perfect gentleman, and straight ahead, you know, you know. But any way, these were beautiful days, and so I left there and I think I joined Slam again. And then I worked Bop City with Slam. And the band playing opposite us there was Elliot Lawrence, and did you ever hear of Elliot Lawrence. Well, then his band was a baritone. You know, the baritone players. He was married to Judy --
